Unlike standard pixel-wise losses that treat all regions equally, this method dynamically prioritizes high-frequency structural information, ensuring that the optimizer focuses on geometrically significant areas during pose alignment [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method dynamically prioritizes high-frequency structural information (edges) to focus the optimizer on geometrically significant areas, unlike standard losses. The evidence confirms that the method uses an 'edge guided loss' which increases the learning rate by 1.5x on edge pixels (detected via Sobel filter) to amplify gradient signals for pose alignment. It explicitly states this helps the joint optimization focus more on the edge area, resulting in more robust pose optimization. The mention of 'dynamic' prioritization is supported by the fact that this edge-guided scale is applied alternately on every other training iteration, and the context contrasts this with standard approaches that suffer from weak/noisy gradients due to aggressive filtering (which destroys edge info). Thus, all facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.
